name: Ouroboros Energy VoltCarriage EC-9 Inductive Roadway Transit Pod
product_name: Ouroboros Energy VoltCarriage EC-9 Inductive Roadway Transit Pod
description:
The VoltCarriage EC-9 is a six-passenger autonomous ground transit pod manufactured in partnership between Ouroboros Energy and Cinderblock AI, designed to operate exclusively on Ouroboros-managed inductive charging roadway segments embedded in Meridian 88's primary arterial corridors. The EC-9 carries no onboard battery system of meaningful capacity — instead, it draws continuous power from a resonant inductive coil array beneath its chassis that couples with Ouroboros's embedded road transmitter grid, receiving up to 180 kW while in motion. This design philosophy eliminates charging downtime entirely but creates absolute dependency on Ouroboros-maintained road infrastructure. The pod's Cinderblock AI piloting system manages platooning formations of up to 12 EC-9 units traveling in coordinated convoys at 110 km/h, reducing aerodynamic drag and increasing per-road-segment passenger throughput significantly.

The EC-9 operates on a subscription transit model: Ouroboros sells route access packages tiered by corridor priority, meaning that a premium subscriber's pod receives uninterrupted inductive power and convoy priority queuing, while a basic-tier pod may experience deliberate power-throttling during peak demand — slowing it to a crawl or forcing it to a holding bay while premium traffic passes. The vehicle's exterior is smooth, low-slung, and visually identical across subscription tiers by deliberate corporate policy, which Ouroboros markets as 'egalitarian design.' The pods communicate continuously with the Saltmarsh Telecom AtmoMesh network for environmental routing adjustments and with the PiezoCore LD-5 grid for energy credit accounting when the pod traverses pedestrian-adjacent surface zones.
base_technologies: Ouroboros Energy PiezoCore LD-5 Pedestrian Kinetic Harvesting Grid
Ouroboros Energy ThermalSink UR-3 District Waste Heat Exchange Network
Saltmarsh Telecom AtmoMesh QL-7 Urban Air Quality Sensor Lattice
social_impact: The VoltCarriage EC-9 has effectively transferred control of Meridian 88's primary road corridors from municipal transit authorities to Ouroboros Energy, since the inductive road segments require Ouroboros maintenance contracts to function and the company retains the right to throttle or deny power to any pod on the network. This has been used at least twice during labor disputes — Ouroboros quietly throttled EC-9 service to districts where union organizing was active, framing the slowdowns as 'infrastructure maintenance.' The subscription model's deliberate visual uniformity masks a deeply hierarchical system: every pod looks the same, but some arrive on time and some spend hours in holding bays, and the difference is entirely determined by ability to pay.
story_hooks: An EC-9 pod carrying a corporate whistleblower is held in a 'maintenance bay' indefinitely — the Cinderblock AI piloting system shows no fault, but the pod simply will not move

Someone has hacked a stretch of Ouroboros inductive road to broadcast power without authentication — free, untracked EC-9 travel on a three-block corridor, and the city is fracturing over who's responsible
A Cinderblock AI platooning convoy of 12 EC-9s detaches from its scheduled route and begins moving in a coordinated formation toward the Ouroboros district headquarters — all pods empty
Ouroboros is bidding to extend inductive road coverage into Tier 3 districts, which sounds like infrastructure investment until someone reads the service agreement's power-throttling clauses
